Breda surrendered in June 1625 after a siege of about nine months.

slides.headline: The loser hands over the keys. Watch the winner.
slides.sub: Diego Velázquez, The Surrender of Breda, 1634-35

slides.text: 1625. After a long siege, the Dutch city of Breda surrenders to the Spanish army. Now the keys of the city must change hands.

slides.headline: The keys
slides.text: In the centre, the Dutch governor, Justin of Nassau, bows and offers the keys of his city to the enemy.

slides.headline: The gesture
slides.text: But the Spanish general, Ambrosio Spinola, lays a hand on his shoulder and stops him from kneeling. Respect, not humiliation.

slides.headline: The lances
slides.text: On the right, the Spanish lances stand straight and proud. That is why Spaniards simply call this painting Las Lanzas.

slides.headline: The horse
slides.text: Spinola's great horse turns its back to us, a bold idea that pulls our eye straight into the scene.

slides.headline: The defeated
slides.text: On the left, the Dutch soldiers look tired and disordered. Some look out at us, as if asking us to judge.

slides.headline: The painter?
slides.text: On the far right, under a big hat, a man looks straight out at us. Many believe he is Velázquez himself.

slides.headline: Your choice
slides.text: Velázquez painted it ten years later, for the king's palace. If you had won, would you let your enemy keep his pride?
